text:
jamie: heads-up, after today's deploy we're seeing a compile-job flood and p95 latency +35% on short-seq workloads. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/runtime/compile-queue
arjun: saw the spike at 12:03UTC, aligns with rollout of PR #4123 (batch splay heuristic)
sasha: starting a quick bisect to find the first bad commit, will post output
arjun: logs show KV cache evictions up ~8x during the spike; prefix cache TTL looks low (60s) in the active config
marta: that's odd — default TTL should be 3600s. PR #4123 diff includes `batching.splay_ttl: 60` and `splay_flush_on_eviction: true`
sasha: bisect output -> first bad commit is a1b2c3d (merge from feature/batch-splay). reproducer attached in my perf run notes

sasha: repro steps:
```
git checkout a1b2c3d
make perf-local TEST=shortseq
# observe compile jobs and `runtime/compile_queue` spike
```

jamie: confirmed locally, compile jobs jump immediately when splay enabled with TTL=60
arjun: suggestion: bump TTL back to 3600 and disable flush-on-eviction while we investigate algorithmic behavior
marta: can we toggle via config flag instead of a full revert? we have a dynamic config rollout path

sasha: opened canary config patch in vault -> set `batching.splay_ttl_seconds: 3600` and `batching.splay_flush_on_eviction: false`
deploy-bot: applying canary config patch to cluster canary-2 (patch id cfg-2024-78)
deploy-bot: canary applied; monitoring

ci-bot: FYI, CI perf job #2345 on master failed with +28% short-seq p95, reproducer job linked: https://ci.redwood/job/2345/logs
arjun: canary metrics look promising — compile queue down ~70% on canary vs prod baseline, p95 trending down

marta: if canary stays stable for 10m we'll roll the config to prod. opening revert PR as a fallback: PR #4130 (revert a1b2c3d)
sasha: also adding a regression test to the autotuner suite: assert compile-queue-rate doesn't increase >2x when splay is toggled, and verify KV eviction rate

jamie: quick note for postmortem: root cause seems to be mismatch between intended TTL and the shipped config plus aggressive flush flag -> caused rapid prefix eviction which forced repeated kernel compilations and bad autopick behavior under short-seq patterns
arjun: long-term action items: (1) add config safeguards for TTL ranges, (2) unit test splay+cache interactions, (3) improve telemetry to show splay churn and kernel compile counts per model
marta: rolling config to prod now (cfg-2024-78 -> prod). will update when rollout finishes
deploy-bot: prod rollout complete across regions, 4/4 clusters successful :thumbsup:

jamie: thanks everyone. please keep this thread for updates, and add any logs/graphs to the follow-up postmortem. tagging infra-oncall for visibility
sasha: I'll attach the bisect log and add the new regression test in the same branch, then link the changelist to the PM postmortem
jamie: good work — let's keep a watch for 24h but I think the immediate rollout blocker is resolved :eyes:
